Discover Grace Dieu

Three Facets of an Extraordinary Monument

Step beyond the ruins to uncover ancient woodland biodiversity, female aristocratic courage, and world-class regional geology.

Nature & Parkland

Explore the Trails

Wander through ancient woodland alongside Grace Dieu Brook. Discover the towering arches of the disused railway viaduct and the remnants of the historic Charnwood Forest canal bed.

Walking Routes & Route Map
Monastic Founder

Roesia’s Legacy

Founded c. 1239 by the formidable Roesia de Verdun, an independent Norman-Irish noblewoman praised by King Henry III. Her tomb still rests in neighbouring Belton church.

Read the Historical Chronicle
UNESCO Aspiration

Charnwood Geopark Partner

As proud partners in the Charnwood Forest Geopark network, our joint working parties recently exposed an 800-year-old boundary wall, supporting the regional UNESCO bid.

Discover the Partnership
Landmark Milestone · November 2024

Permanent Ownership Secured by the Grace Dieu Priory Trust

After two years of detailed negotiations with private landowners, our parent organisation, The Grace Dieu Priory Trust, purchased the freehold title to the ruins and Rusty Mary’s field. Having previously looked after the ancient monument as tenants, freehold ownership secures its preservation for generations to come, unlocking opportunities for scheduled archaeological excavations and a permanent footbridge.

Read the BBC News Report Coverage originally broadcast by BBC East Midlands
Community Volunteer Appeal

A few hours a year keeps the Priory open.

Whether you have office and secretarial skills, digital know-how, or can help raise a gazebo and steward parking during our summer fayre, we need your help.

The founding volunteer committee is aging and struggling to maintain the necessary activity levels. We are not locking the gates tomorrow, but without new volunteer blood, the future of this public sanctuary is at risk. You will be warmly welcomed!

Visitor Code

Leave No TracePlease take all of your litter home with you. There are no public waste bins on the ancient monument ruins.
Dog WalkersDogs welcome on leads. A dedicated bin is located at the Bull's Head car park for dog litter bags (strictly none on-site).
Strict Site Policy: Paranormal events and ghost walks are expressly forbidden by the Grace Dieu Priory Trust across the entire priory site and surrounding lands.
